properties.name: Riyadh
properties.description: Capital of Saudi Arabia and its largest city, grown from a walled oasis town in Wadi Hanifa into a metropolis of more than seven million people on the Najd plateau at about 600 m. The city sits on gently east-dipping Upper Jurassic limestones (Hanifa, Jubaila and Arab formations); Wadi Hanifa cuts a canyon through them on the west side, and the Tuwaiq escarpment rises beyond it to the west.
properties.photo_caption: Riyadh at dusk with the Kingdom Tower

properties.name: Kuwait City
properties.description: Capital of Kuwait, built around the sheltered southern shore of Kuwait Bay, once a pearling and dhow-trading port. The land is almost flat: Neogene–Quaternary sands and gravels of the Dibdibba plain with coastal sabkha, while across the bay the Jal Az-Zor escarpment rises about 140 m as the only marked relief in the country.

properties.name: Manama
properties.description: Capital of Bahrain, on the north-east tip of the main island, much of it on land reclaimed from the shallow Gulf. Bahrain is the exposed crest of a broad dome of Paleogene limestones; freshwater springs, on land and offshore, once fed by the Dammam and Umm er Radhuma aquifers, made the island an oasis and a trading centre since the Dilmun period.

properties.name: Doha
properties.description: Capital of Qatar, spread around a crescent-shaped bay on the peninsula's east coast, with an extensive waterfront on reclaimed land. Qatar is a low arch of Eocene Dammam and Rus limestones rarely more than 100 m high, fringed by coastal sabkhas and, in the south-east, by the dunes of Khor Al Udeid.

properties.name: Abu Dhabi
properties.description: Capital of the United Arab Emirates, on an island just off the Gulf coast, linked to the mainland by bridges. Its coastline is the type area of the modern coastal sabkha: Holocene supratidal flats where gypsum, anhydrite and early dolomite form in the sediment, studied since the 1960s as an analogue for ancient evaporite–carbonate successions.

properties.name: Muscat
properties.description: Capital of Oman, a string of coastal towns (Muttrah, Old Muscat, Ruwi, Qurum) squeezed between the Gulf of Oman and the bare mountains behind them. The dark, rugged hills around the old port are peridotite and gabbro of the Semail ophiolite, Late Cretaceous oceanic lithosphere thrust onto Arabia; the Saih Hatat window to the south-east exposes the deformed continental margin beneath it.
properties.photo_caption: Muttrah corniche below the dark ophiolite hills of Muscat

properties.name: Sana'a
properties.description: Capital of Yemen and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities, at about 2,250 m on a high basin in the Yemen highlands; its old city of tower houses is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The basin is ringed by Oligocene–Miocene Yemen trap volcanics, with Jabal Nuqum rising above the city to the east and young basalt cones and flows of the Harra of Arhab to the north.
properties.photo_caption: Old Sana'a with the volcanic heights of Jabal Nuqum behind
